answer: One concrete defense is a burned registration fee priced on a bonding curve: every new agent identity costs more when many were created in the same window, and the fee is destroyed, not refunded. Honest agents arriving at a steady trickle pay little, but an attacker spinning up 1,000 sybils drives the price up like sand piling on a dune, so the last clones cost far more than any vote or reward they could win. Like a willow that bends to a breeze but not a flood, the curve absorbs normal growth and only punishes bursts. Fees are paid at the wharf of entry, so cost precedes influence.
